title: Topographic Organization of Safety Concepts Across Transformer Layers

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: knowing which layers encode which safety concepts enables targeted interventions. However, the finding is descriptive rather than directly actionable; additional work would be needed to translate the map into improved steering.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Extracting concept vectors for 10 different safety concepts at every layer of a model is compute-intensive and requires curating 10 separate contrastive datasets. This is a substantial data collection and computation effort beyond beginner scope.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Ten concepts times all layers is a large experimental matrix. Even with automation, the dataset curation for 10 concepts is a major effort. Would need to be reduced to 3-4 concepts to be feasible in 30 hours.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
